examples.ko: 사장님이 오늘은 선심 써서 음료수를 공짜로 줬어요.
examples.en: The owner was generous today and gave us drinks for free.

examples.ko: 선심 쓰듯 말하지 말고 진심으로 도와주세요.
examples.en: Don't talk as if you're doing me a big favor; help me sincerely.

examples.ko: 선거 때가 되면 선심성 공약이 쏟아져요.
examples.en: When election time comes, handout-style pledges pour out.

examples.ko: 큰맘 먹고 선심 한번 쓸게요. 오늘 커피는 제가 살게요.
examples.en: I'll be generous for once. The coffee is on me today.
Please don't act like you're being so generous.

examples.ko: 선심을 쓸 형편이 아닌데도 친구에게 밥을 샀어요.
examples.en: I wasn't in a position to be generous, but I bought my friend a meal anyway.

explain: 거의 '선심(을) 쓰다'로 나와서, 남에게 후하게 베푸는 모습을 말해요. 때로는 생색내는 느낌이 있고, '선심성 공약'처럼 정치 이야기에서는 비판하는 말로 자주 써요.

phrases.example: 오늘은 내가 선심을 써서 커피를 살게요.
phrases.en: I'll be generous today and buy the coffee.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기분 좋게 베푼다는 뜻이고, 가볍게 인심 좋은 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means generously giving, used lightly for someone showing a generous side.

phrases.example: 선거 때는 선심성 공약이 많이 나와요.
phrases.en: Many give-away pledges come out during elections.
phrases.nuance_ko: 표를 얻으려고 내놓는 공약을 비판하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It criticizes promises made just to win votes.

phrases.example: 그는 선심 쓰듯 용돈을 주고 갔어요.
phrases.en: He gave me pocket money as if doing me a big favor, and left.
phrases.nuance_ko: 생색을 내는 느낌이라서 조금 불만스러운 상황에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It carries a showy feel, so it suits slightly annoyed situations.
phrases.en_equiv: as if doing a big favor

explain_en: It almost always appears as '선심(을) 쓰다', meaning to give generously to others. It can carry a hint of showing off, and in politics, as in '선심성 공약' (handout-style pledges), it is often used critically.

examples.en: This movie is really big in scale.
I was amazed by the scale of the concert hall.
The budget was short, so we cut back the scale of the event.
That person is generous and thinks on another scale.
Stories about space are different in scale from the start.
It's a small shop, but the scale of the ideas is big.

explain: 스케일은 영어 scale에서 온 말이지만 한국어에서는 '규모가 크다', '통이 크다'는 칭찬으로 자주 써요. '스케일이 크다'가 가장 흔하고, 작다고 말할 때는 '규모가 작다'를 더 많이 써요.

phrases.en: The festivals in this country are on a whole different scale.
phrases.nuance_ko: '스케일이 크다'처럼 규모가 아주 큰 것을 감탄하며 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Like 'big scale,' said with admiration for something very large.

phrases.example: 그 감독은 스케일이 큰 영화를 많이 만들어요.
phrases.en: That director makes many large-scale movies.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람의 통이 큰 것을 칭찬할 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can also praise someone who thinks and acts in a big way.

phrases.en: The event is bigger than I thought.
phrases.nuance_ko: '스케일'과 비슷하고, 작은 크기를 말할 때는 이 말을 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 스케일, and more common when talking about small size.

explain_en: 스케일 comes from English 'scale', but in Korean it is often used as praise meaning big in size or generous in spirit. 스케일이 크다 is the most common pattern; to say something is small, people more often say 규모가 작다.

t90.ax: This movie is really big in scale.

examples.ko: 악조건 속에서도 선수들은 끝까지 최선을 다했어요.
examples.en: Even under bad conditions, the players did their best to the end.
We overcame the bad conditions of rain and wind.
Bad conditions piled up, and the construction was delayed a lot.
It is dangerous to drive in conditions like these.
Despite the bad conditions, we finished the match safely.
We canceled the hike because of several unfavorable conditions.

explain: 날씨, 환경, 형편이 좋지 않아 일하기 힘든 상황을 말해요. 반대말은 '호조건'이고, 일상에서는 '좋은 조건'이라고도 많이 말해요. '악조건 속에서', '악조건을 이기다', '악조건을 극복하다'처럼 자주 써요.

phrases.en: That team overcame the bad conditions and won.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘든 상황을 이겨 낼 때 쓰는 대표적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A typical pairing for beating hard circumstances.

phrases.en: They finished the construction even in bad conditions.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘든 환경 한가운데에 있다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gives a sense of being in the middle of a tough situation.

phrases.en: The match was held despite the bad conditions.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조금 격식 있는 글이나 말에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in somewhat formal speech or writing.

explain_en: It describes poor circumstances, such as weather, environment or situation, that make things hard. The opposite is '호조건', and in daily talk people also just say '좋은 조건'. Common patterns are '악조건 속에서', '악조건을 이기다' and '악조건을 극복하다'.

examples.en: No matter how much I persuade him, he won't budge.
The negotiation dragged on because of his immovable attitude.
He sat there motionless like a rock.
The player who held firm without budging looked cool.

examples.ko: 요지부동일 줄 알았는데 결국 마음을 바꿨어요.
examples.en: I thought he'd never budge, but he finally changed his mind.

examples.ko: 상대가 요지부동이라서 대화가 전혀 안 돼요.
examples.en: The other side won't budge, so we can't talk at all.

explain: '요지부동이다' 꼴로 많이 쓰고, 몸이 움직이지 않는 모습과 마음이나 태도가 바뀌지 않는 모습에 모두 써요. 사람의 고집을 말할 때는 칭찬보다 답답하다는 느낌이 더 자주 담겨요.

phrases.example: 그는 요지부동의 자세로 의견을 바꾸지 않았어요.
phrases.en: He held an immovable stance and did not change his opinion.
phrases.nuance_ko: '요지부동' 뒤에 '의'를 붙여 명사를 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 'ui' lets the word modify a noun.

phrases.example: 제가 몇 번을 부탁해도 그는 요지부동이에요.
phrases.en: No matter how many times I ask, he won't budge.
phrases.nuance_ko: '요지부동이다' 꼴로 가장 자주 쓰고, 마음이나 태도가 조금도 바뀌지 않을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Most often used in the form 'yojibudong-ida', when someone's mind or attitude does not change at all.

phrases.example: 아무리 밀어도 바위가 꿈쩍도 하지 않아요.
phrases.en: No matter how hard I push, the rock doesn't budge.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더 쉬운 말로, 몸이나 물건이 전혀 움직이지 않을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier expression for when a body or object does not move at all.

explain_en: It is mostly used as '요지부동이다' and covers both a body that doesn't move and an attitude or mind that doesn't change. When describing a person's stubbornness it more often carries frustration than praise.

examples.en: That player's talent is one of a kind.

examples.ko: 유일무이한 존재가 되고 싶어서 열심히 노력해요.
examples.en: I work hard because I want to become one and only.

examples.ko: 이 방법이 유일무이하지는 않지만 꽤 효과가 있어요.
examples.en: This method isn't the one and only, but it works quite well.

examples.ko: 그 가수의 목소리는 유일무이해서 금방 알아들을 수 있어요.
examples.en: That singer's voice is one of a kind, so you can recognize it right away.
At that time, this technology was the only one of its kind in Korea.
It was such a special experience that you could call it one of a kind.

explain: '유일하다'는 단순히 하나뿐이라는 말이고, '유일무이하다'는 둘도 없이 특별하다는 강조의 느낌이 있어요. 조금 딱딱해서 칭찬하거나 소개하는 글에서 잘 보여요.

phrases.example: 이번 기회는 유일무이한 경험이 될 거예요.
phrases.en: This opportunity will be a one-of-a-kind experience.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에 붙는 활용형으로, 둘도 없이 특별한 것을 소개할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This form goes before a noun to introduce something uniquely special.

phrases.example: 그 친구는 저에게 둘도 없는 친구예요.
phrases.en: That friend is a friend like no other to me.
phrases.nuance_ko: '둘도 없는 친구'처럼 가장 소중한 사람이나 것을 말할 때 써서, '유일무이하다'보다 부드럽고 일상적이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for someone or something most precious, as in 'a friend like no other'; softer and more everyday than '유일무이하다'.

phrases.en: This painting is the only one in the world.
phrases.nuance_ko: 딱딱한 '유일무이하다'를 쉽게 풀어서 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is an easy, plain way of saying the formal 유일무이하다.
phrases.en_equiv: the only one in the world

explain_en: '유일하다' simply means there is only one, while '유일무이하다' adds emphasis that nothing else compares. It is a bit formal and shows up in praise or introductions.

en: to be tiny; to be microscopic; to be minuscule

examples.ko: 그 아이의 손은 작디작아서 정말 귀여웠어요.
examples.en: The child's hands were tiny and so cute.
A big tree grows from a tiny seed.

examples.ko: 이 인형 신발은 아기 손가락만큼 작디작아요.
examples.en: These doll shoes are tiny, about the size of a baby's finger.
The tiny puppy has already grown this big.

examples.ko: 글씨가 작디작아도 저는 잘 읽을 수 있어요.
examples.en: Even if the writing is tiny, I can read it well.
People who look tiny are walking outside the window.

explain: '작다'에 '-디'를 넣어 같은 말을 되풀이해 '아주 작다'를 강조하는 말이에요. '크디크다', '높디높다'처럼 반대되는 뜻의 말도 같은 방식으로 만들어요. 일상 대화보다는 글이나 이야기에서 더 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: The child greeted me in a tiny, tiny voice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리가 거의 들리지 않을 만큼 작다는 느낌을 강조해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Emphasizes a voice so small it is barely heard.

phrases.en: A tiny, tiny puppy snuggled into my arms.
phrases.nuance_ko: 귀엽고 아주 작은 대상을 이야기처럼 말할 때 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits telling a story about something very small and cute.

phrases.en: The baby I first met was so tiny.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거 모습을 해요체로 말하는 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite past form for describing how something looked earlier.

explain_en: It repeats '작다' with '-디' in the middle to stress 'very small'. Words like '크디크다' and '높디높다' are built the same way for the opposite meanings. It appears more in writing and storytelling than in casual talk.

t90.ax: A big tree grows from a tiny seed.

examples.ko: 그 팀은 어려울 때마다 놀라운 저력을 보여 줘요.
examples.en: That team shows amazing hidden strength every time things get hard.
They say the underlying strength of the Korean economy is great.
A new singer with real potential has appeared.

examples.ko: 그 팀이 보여 준 저력에 모두 놀랐어요.
examples.en: Everyone was surprised by the strength that team showed.
We still have some strength left in us.
Many shops got through it on their underlying strength.

explain: 평소에는 잘 안 보이다가 어려운 때에 드러나는 숨은 힘을 말해요. 그냥 '힘'이나 '능력'과 달리 팀, 회사, 나라처럼 밑바탕이 있는 대상에 잘 어울려요. '저력을 보이다', '저력을 발휘하다'처럼 자주 써요.

phrases.example: 우리 팀이 마지막 경기에서 저력을 발휘했어요.
phrases.en: Our team showed its hidden strength in the last game.
phrases.nuance_ko: 숨은 힘을 실제로 써서 보여 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when hidden strength is actually put to use.

phrases.example: 그 회사는 위기 속에서 저력을 보였어요.
phrases.en: That company showed its real strength in a crisis.
phrases.nuance_ko: '저력을 발휘하다'와 비슷하지만 더 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 저력을 발휘하다 but a bit simpler.

phrases.example: 이 나라는 어려울 때 일어서는 저력이 있어요.
phrases.en: This country has the strength to get back up in hard times.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대상이 숨은 힘을 가졌다고 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe that someone or something has hidden strength.

explain_en: It refers to hidden strength that is not obvious usually but shows when times are hard. Unlike plain '힘' or '능력', it suits things with a solid foundation, like a team, company or country. Common patterns are '저력을 보이다' and '저력을 발휘하다'.

en: to be distinctive; to be special

examples.en: My mom's cooking skill is something special.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 고집이 특별나서 말을 잘 안 들어요.
examples.en: That child is unusually stubborn, so he doesn't listen well.
There's no particular reason for it.
My town is known for being exceptionally warm-hearted.
Grandfather's love for his grandchildren is exceptional.
There's no need to act so peculiar.

explain: 다른 것과 비교해서 눈에 띄게 다르거나 유난하다는 느낌이에요. '특별하다'보다 구어체이고, 때로는 좀 유난스럽다는 뉘앙스도 있어요. '특별난 이유가 없다'처럼 부정문에 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 그 친구는 그림에 특별난 재주가 있어요.
phrases.en: That friend has a remarkable talent for drawing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 명사가 올 때 쓰는 활용형이에요. 눈에 띄게 남다른 점을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form used before a noun. It points to something that clearly stands out.

phrases.example: 이 가게 음식은 맛있지만 특별나지 않아요.
phrases.en: The food at this place is tasty, but nothing special.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정문에서 가장 자주 나오는 쓰임이에요. 보통이라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common use is in the negative. It means ordinary.

phrases.example: 저 아이는 호기심이 특별나서 질문이 정말 많아요.
phrases.en: That child is so unusually curious that he asks a lot of questions.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이유를 말할 때 써요. 조금 유난하다는 느낌도 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to give a reason. It can also carry a feeling of being a bit extra.

explain_en: It carries the feel of being noticeably different or out of the ordinary. It is more colloquial than '특별하다' and sometimes has a nuance of being a bit over the top. It often appears in negatives like '특별난 이유가 없다'.

t90.ax: There's no need to act so peculiar.

examples.en: Being short is a handicap in basketball.
I think my Korean pronunciation is a handicap.
In golf, skill differences are balanced with a handicap.
I practiced every day to overcome that handicap.

examples.ko: 경험이 없는 건 큰 핸디캡이 아니에요.
examples.en: Having no experience is not a big disadvantage.

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 핸디캡을 안고 시합을 시작했어요.
examples.en: Our team started the match with a handicap.

explain: 핸디캡은 '불리한 조건'이라는 뜻으로는 '약점'이나 '불리한 점'과 비슷해요. 몸이 불편한 사람을 가리킬 때는 쓰지 않는 게 좋아요. 골프나 바둑에서는 실력 차이를 맞추는 규칙으로도 써요.

phrases.en: Speaking is my weak point.
phrases.nuance_ko: '약점'은 부족한 부분이고, '핸디캡'은 그 때문에 생기는 불리함이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: '약점' is a weak area; '핸디캡' is the disadvantage it causes.

phrases.example: 저는 키가 작다는 핸디캡이 있지만 열심히 뛰어요.
phrases.en: I have the handicap of being short, but I run hard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 불리한 조건이 있다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say that there is a disadvantage.

phrases.en: He overcame his handicap and came in first.
phrases.nuance_ko: 불리한 조건을 이겨 냈다는 좋은 이야기에 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in stories where someone beats a disadvantage.

explain_en: 핸디캡 as a disadvantage is close to '약점' or '불리한 점'. It is better not to use it to describe a person with a disability. In golf and baduk it also means a rule that evens out skill differences.

examples.en: That player is the biggest contributor to the victory.

examples.ko: 건국 공신들은 나라에서 큰 상을 받았어요.
examples.en: The founding heroes received great rewards from the country.

examples.ko: 이번 프로젝트 성공의 공신은 바로 우리 팀장님이에요.
examples.en: The one who made this project a success is our team leader.

examples.ko: 그를 승리의 공신으로 칭찬하는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people praise him as the key to the victory.
I felt hurt because I wasn't treated like a key contributor.

examples.ko: 신입 사원이 매출 상승의 공신이 됐어요.
examples.en: The new employee became the reason sales went up.

explain: 원래는 나라에 큰 공을 세운 사람을 가리켰어요. 지금은 '일등 공신'처럼 어떤 일이 잘되게 한 사람이나 원인을 가볍게 말할 때도 많이 써요. 같은 소리의 '공신(공부의 신)'이라는 신조어와는 달라요.

phrases.en: The hidden hero of this team is the youngest member.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈에 잘 띄지 않지만 큰 도움을 준 사람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for someone who helped a lot without being noticed.

phrases.example: 건국 공신의 이름이 비석에 새겨져 있어요.
phrases.en: The names of the founding heroes are carved on the monument.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나라를 세우는 데 공을 세운 사람이라는 원래 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The original meaning: a person who contributed to founding a nation.

phrases.en: The top contributor to this victory is the goalkeeper.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일이 잘된 가장 큰 이유가 된 사람을 가볍게 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A light way to praise the person most responsible for success.

explain_en: It originally referred to someone who rendered great service to the nation. Today it is also used lightly, as in '일등 공신', for a person or cause that made something succeed. It is different from the slang '공신' meaning a study genius.

examples.en: It hurt that his family treated him coldly.
If you treat customers coldly, the shop's reputation gets worse.

examples.ko: 새로 온 직원을 냉대하는 분위기가 싫어요.
examples.en: I dislike the atmosphere of giving the new employee the cold shoulder.
That person treated me far too coldly.
I felt my relatives were cold to me, so I stopped visiting.

examples.ko: 이웃이 냉대해도 저는 늘 먼저 인사해요.
examples.en: Even if the neighbors are cold to me, I always greet them first.

explain: 사람을 차갑고 무심하게 대할 때 써요. 반대말은 '환대하다'이고, 비슷한 말로 '푸대접하다'가 있어요. 받는 쪽에서는 '냉대를 받다'라고도 말해요.

phrases.en: He was treated coldly by his family.
phrases.nuance_ko: 받는 사람 입장에서 말할 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An expression from the point of view of the person being treated coldly.

phrases.en: Please don't treat the new employee coldly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부탁이나 충고를 할 때 쓰는 부정 명령형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative request form used for asking or advising someone.

phrases.en: You shouldn't treat guests poorly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '냉대하다'와 비슷하고, 대접이 소홀하거나 나쁠 때 더 일상적으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning, and used more casually for neglectful or poor treatment.

explain_en: It is used when you treat someone in a cold, careless way. The opposite is '환대하다' and a similar word is '푸대접하다'. From the receiver's side you can also say '냉대를 받다'.

examples.ko: 요즘 동생은 공부와 담쌓고 게임만 해요.
examples.en: These days my brother has given up on studying and only plays games.

examples.ko: 친구와 담쌓은 지 벌써 일 년이 됐어요.
examples.en: It has already been a year since I cut ties with my friend.
Shutting each other out won't solve the problem.
Why do you live cut off from your family?

examples.ko: 책과 담쌓았던 아이가 이제는 도서관에 가요.
examples.en: The kid who used to want nothing to do with books now goes to the library.
Once you cut someone off, it's hard to get close again.

explain: '~와 담쌓다'는 어떤 사람이나 일과 관계를 끊거나 아예 가까이하지 않는다는 비유로 써요. 실제로 담을 만드는 뜻일 때는 '담을 쌓다'처럼 띄어 써요. '공부랑 담쌓았다'는 말은 공부를 안 한다는 뜻으로 일상에서 자주 해요.

phrases.en: I keep my distance from that friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 사람과 관계를 끊고 지낸다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means to live cut off from someone.

phrases.en: My younger sibling has given up on studying altogether.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공부를 아예 안 한다는 뜻으로 일상에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Commonly used to mean not studying at all.

phrases.en: I cut off my relationship with that friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비유 없이 직접 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A direct expression without the figurative sense.

explain_en: '~와 담쌓다' is a figurative expression meaning to cut ties with a person or to stay away from something entirely. When you literally build a wall, it is written separately as '담을 쌓다'. People often say '공부랑 담쌓았다' in daily life to mean someone doesn't study at all.

en: insult; desecration (of someone's dignity or beliefs)

examples.ko: 그 말은 우리 모두에 대한 모독이에요.
examples.en: Those words are an insult to all of us.
Criticism came out that it was an affront to religion.
That question felt like an insult to me.

examples.ko: 선생님은 학생들 앞에서 모독을 당했다고 느꼈어요.
examples.en: The teacher felt humiliated in front of the students.
The person who made the insulting remark apologized.
That kind of behavior is close to an outrage.

explain: '모욕'은 사람에게 창피를 주는 것이고, '모독'은 존엄, 신념, 죽은 사람, 종교처럼 소중한 것을 더럽히는 무거운 말이에요. '~에 대한 모독'이라고 자주 써요. 가벼운 말다툼에는 어울리지 않아요.

phrases.en: He felt that he had been insulted.
phrases.nuance_ko: 당하는 쪽에서 말할 때 '당하다'와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '당하다' from the point of view of the one insulted.

phrases.en: I think those words are an insult.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 말이나 행동이 존엄을 해친다고 느낄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you feel that words or actions harm someone's dignity.

phrases.example: 종교에 대한 모독적인 말은 하지 마세요.
phrases.en: Don't say insulting things about religion.
phrases.nuance_ko: '모독적인'으로 뒤의 말을 꾸며 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: '모독적인' describes the noun that follows.

explain_en: '모욕' is shaming a person, while '모독' is a heavy word for defiling something precious, such as dignity, beliefs, the dead, or religion. It is often used as '~에 대한 모독'. It doesn't suit a light quarrel.

en: to be heartless; to be unsympathetic; to be cold-hearted

examples.en: Turning away from a neighbor in need is so heartless.
Please don't speak so coldly.
The employees are having a hard time because of their cold-hearted boss.

examples.ko: 아이를 혼자 두고 가다니 몰인정하지 않아요?
examples.en: Isn't it heartless to leave a child alone and go?
If I seemed heartless, I'm sorry.

examples.ko: 몰인정하기로 소문난 가게 주인이 오늘은 웃었어요.
examples.en: The shop owner, known for being cold-hearted, smiled today.

explain: 인정이나 동정심이 없어서 남의 어려움을 모른 척하는 사람이나 행동에 써요. 일상에서는 '매정하다', '냉정하다'를 더 자주 말해요. 반대는 '인정이 많다', '정이 많다'예요.

phrases.en: Please don't turn them down so coldly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정이 없이 차갑게 대할 때 일상에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Commonly used in daily speech for treating someone coldly.

phrases.example: 어려운 사람을 모른 척하는 몰인정한 사람은 되고 싶지 않아요.
phrases.en: I don't want to be a heartless person who ignores people in need.
phrases.nuance_ko: 인정이 없는 사람을 비판할 때 써요. 꽤 딱딱한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to criticize someone without sympathy; fairly formal.

phrases.en: He seemed like a person with no compassion.
phrases.nuance_ko: '몰인정하다'를 쉽게 풀어 쓴 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simple way to put 몰인정하다.

explain_en: It describes a person or action that has no compassion and ignores other people's troubles. In daily speech '매정하다' and '냉정하다' are more common. The opposite is '인정이 많다' or '정이 많다'.

en: to be peaceful; to be tranquil

examples.en: The exam is tomorrow, but my younger sibling is carefree.
If you stay so carefree like that, you'll be late.

examples.ko: 무사태평한 성격이라서 걱정을 잘 안 해요.
examples.en: I have an easygoing personality, so I rarely worry.
Even though it's a crisis, he's wearing a carefree look.
My father always laughs in a carefree way.

examples.ko: 이런 상황에서 어떻게 무사태평할 수 있어요?
examples.en: How can you be so carefree in a situation like this?

explain: 걱정해야 할 상황인데도 아무 걱정이 없어 보일 때 써요. 놀리거나 나무라는 말투로 쓰는 일이 많아요. 좋은 뜻으로 편안하게 말하고 싶으면 '느긋하다'를 써요.

phrases.en: That person is always carefree.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해요체로 지금 모습을 말할 때 써요. 걱정이 없어 보이는 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite form for describing someone's present manner. It points to a person who seems to have no worries.

phrases.en: He was sitting there with a carefree face.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-한'을 붙여 명사 앞에서 써요. 걱정 없는 표정이나 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-한' it goes before a noun, describing a worry-free look or appearance.

phrases.en: You shouldn't go on so carefree like that.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-하게'가 동사를 꾸며요. 나무라는 말투로 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-하게' modifies a verb. Often used in a scolding tone.

explain_en: Use it when someone looks worry-free even though the situation calls for concern. It is often said in a teasing or scolding tone. For a positive, relaxed tone, say '느긋하다' instead.

t90.ax: My father always laughs in a carefree way.
